A user of several months said Helicone helped them solve a bug with OpenAI's API. Requests were failing and some responses weren't being logged, and Helicone quickly showed it was a token limit issue. They also liked the integration: 'just one line to swap out the OpenAI API with theirs.'
"onboarded and started using it in literally 2 minutes. nice"
Happy Helicone customer: "It's a dead simple setup. It's great to have the extra charts and logging to debug issues and make sure all is running well."

A LangChain user said that when chains get long or complex, debug output makes it hard to see the final prompt actually sent, its cost, or runaway agents. Helicone 'pretty much solves that for me.' They were up and running in 4 minutes, and asked for a way to see and export all prompts and responses over time to tune them.

Feature gap: a user wants to store the template and parameters that produced each concrete prompt. Custom Properties allow only a little metadata, not a big blob like a template. They don't want Helicone doing the template substitution because they have particular templating needs. They also asked for per-user/app maximum cost blocking.

Pricing complaint: "the jump in cost from Free to Starter will keep me from using this for my own projects, 1000 requests just isn't that much, and if I'm doing something more serious then 50,000 requests also doesn't seem like a lot."

Comparison with OpenAI's dashboard: OpenAI shows little beyond 'total cost per day.' "I like that Helicone allows me to see each request and export them all, so that I can use that to build my fine-tuning dataset."
Security concern about the proxy design: "Hmm, so to integrate I have to basically send my api key to you on every request? Not great"
Commenters questioned whether proxying OpenAI traffic through a commercial broker could violate OpenAI's ToS and put users' access at risk. One called the approach 'pretty brittle.'

Privacy/compliance concern: PII from end-users could leak if usage isn't disclosed and consented. EU end-users may require new informed consent. Another user suggested adding Helicone to your GDPR subprocessor list as a workaround.

A commenter noted Helicone called itself open source while using the Commons Clause, which isn't typically considered an open source license, and raised it on GitHub. Another pointed out the team had committed an env file in a PR.
Users pointed to simpler open-source alternatives for OpenAI proxying/caching, such as openai-caching-proxy-worker and egoist/openai-proxy.
"This is exactly what we needed. We were one day away from an internal build out so the timing couldn't be better."

On Helicone letting users write SQL directly against a shared ClickHouse, a commenter worried about noisy neighbors: "Its really easy to write a bad query which can drastically slow down the DB."
